approach: Add one reading check, `check_defined_terms(reading, request)`, in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs. It is one `step!` line in `refusing_check`, placed after `check_environment_reach` and before `check_boundary_and_repo_files`. A small const lists the structural words (ladder, rung, tier, layer). `request_words` already splits text into lowercase whole words, so `structural_terms_in` reuses it; plurals and `'s` map to the base word, and `stepladder` and `delayer` do not match. For each word the request uses, the reading must have (a) a summary line or assumption that starts `Term <word>:` followed by at least 4 words saying what it ranks or does, and (b) a criterion of kind behavior that names the word as a whole word. If not, the check bails with "the reading was refused because ..." and gives both repairs. `read_for` already sends that text to the reader for its one re-read, so the reader prompt needs no change. It skips a reading with no capability or with a question. A doc comment names the root cause, jobs 7bf8 and 0wtc, the limits, and "expected 3% of newly refused readings". The tests are corpus cases in refusal_corpus.rs and unit tests in reading.rs. The replay test over the three cited requests is rewritten: g6vy is caught by check_outcome_state, 7bf8 by check_defined_terms, and 0wtc holds no structural word and is asserted as outside the class. The old check_outcome_state doc, its test needles, and the old CHANGELOG sentence "are not caught" are corrected. A rule line is added to READING_RULES in briefs.rs, which is brief text and not the budgeted prompt, so the reader is told up front. The change is recorded in CHANGELOG.md and as a new decision D164 that amends D161 in prose, because the log is append-only.

decisions.choice: Fix at reading acceptance: a new `step!(check_defined_terms(reading, request))` in `refusing_check`, which is where a reading is first accepted without being checked against what the user observes. Do not patch one job's request.
decisions.reason: The shared cause is that `check_reading_acceptance` takes request wording on faith. `check_outcome_state` (reading.rs:3680) covers only four delivery verbs, and its doc names the other two jobs as uncovered. One new step covers the whole structural-term class with no new plumbing, and the corpus mechanism (`every_acceptance_check_has_a_refusing_corpus_case`) forces a case for it.

rejected.option: Extend check_outcome_state's verb list with ladder, tier and similar
rejected.why: They are nouns that rank things, not delivery verbs. The repair differs (a definition plus an observable test, not a reachable state), and that function's rules and tests are out of scope beyond its doc.

rejected.option: Read docs/ontology.toml at reading time and check against the glossary
rejected.why: It needs new plumbing and touches the rejected 0wtc ontology work, which is out of scope. A const list is enough for now.

rejected.option: Judge definitions with a model call or in the verifier
rejected.why: The verifier sees the problem only after the producer has run. A lexical check costs no call and can be tested in the corpus.

decisions.choice: Place the step right after `check_environment_reach` and before `check_boundary_and_repo_files`.
decisions.reason: Existing tests pin neighbours: `check_outcome_state_doc_names_root_cause_and_scope` pins outcome_state right after governance, and `environment_reach_has_one_step_line` pins environment_reach right after outcome_state. Placing the new step after environment_reach breaks neither. The check reads only the reading and the request, so it sits before the file-comparing checks.

rejected.why: It would make `environment_reach_has_one_step_line` (reading.rs:8856) fail, which needs an unrelated test edit.

decisions.choice: Matching: terms are ladder, rung, tier, layer. A request word counts if it equals the term, term+`s`, or either with `'s` (via `request_words`, which splits on `-`). A definition is a summary line or assumption whose lowercase text starts `term <word>:` with at least 4 words after the colon. A criterion counts only if its kind is Behavior and it names the word as a whole word. The check skips a reading with no capability or with a question.
decisions.reason: Whole-word matching keeps `stepladder` and `delayer` accepted (criterion 2). Plurals (`three tiers`) are the same misread. Requiring 4 words stops a bare `Term ladder: yes`. A content criterion can be met by a Grep on a file, which is the g6vy lesson, so only behavior counts. The skip mirrors check_outcome_state.

rejected.option: Accept an out_of_scope item as an exemption, as check_outcome_state does
rejected.why: The accepted reading gives two repairs only: define the term, and give a behavior criterion that names it.
It would refuse `stepladder` and `delayer`, which criterion 2 requires to pass.
`two tiers` would pass undefined. The extra refusal is small and is counted in the declared 3% estimate.

decisions.choice: Expose `pub fn structural_terms_in(request: &str) -> Vec<&'static str>` (unique words, in order) from reading.rs for the corpus replay test.
decisions.reason: Criterion 8 requires the test to assert that 0wtc's request holds no structural word and is outside the class. That count must come from the production matcher, not a copy of it in the test.

rejected.why: It would not follow the matcher if the list changes.

decisions.choice: Add one rule line to `READING_RULES` in crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs and update its test, instead of editing the budgeted reader prompt.
decisions.reason: briefs.rs is a listed deliverable. The rule list is brief text outside the budgeted prompt sets (docs/system-facts.md: briefs sit outside the sets), so the 3 tokens left in the reader prompt do not matter. check_environment_reach did the same. The reader then learns the rule on its first read, not only from the refusal.

rejected.why: The brief gives no room and lists prompt text as out of scope.

rejected.option: No reader rule line, as D161 did
rejected.why: A listed deliverable lets the producer tell the reader up front, so fewer readings burn their one re-read.

decisions.choice: Record the change as a new entry D164 appended to docs/decisions.md, amending D161 in prose, and correct the old Unreleased CHANGELOG sentence 'are not caught' for the first of the two jobs.
decisions.reason: The decision log is append-only: the mirror rule `DecisionEntries` and `decision_log_problems` judge entries after the base. D161 says the other two jobs are not caught and cannot be edited, so D164 states the new scope. The CHANGELOG entry is still Unreleased, so correcting it is allowed.

demonstrations.method: Corpus cases drive the production gate `refusing_check`, the function `check_reading_acceptance` wraps (reading.rs:3228). Case `structural-term-ladder-undefined-is-refused` uses the verbatim 7bf8 request, now a shared const `BF8_REQUEST`, which `CITED_REQUESTS` reuses. Its reading is `base_reading(request)`: a docs reading with a content criterion, which the existing replay test shows passes every earlier check. It expects `Expected::Refuse("check_defined_terms")`. Case `structural-term-ladder-defined-with-a-behavior-criterion-is-accepted` is the same request. The helper `with_behavior` adds a Behavior criterion naming ladder, and the case pushes the assumption 'Term ladder: ranks requirements from the owner goals down to implementation, and a role may change only rungs at or below its limit'. It expects Accept. Two more cases isolate each half: a definition with no behavior criterion is refused, and a behavior criterion with no definition is refused. Matching unit tests in reading.rs cover the summary-line definition, the too-short definition, and a content criterion that names the word.
demonstrations.command: cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus corpus_cases_get_the_expected_outcome; cargo test -p athena-core check_defined_terms
demonstrations.observes: `corpus_cases_get_the_expected_outcome` runs `mismatches(&cases())`. The undefined case is refused by check_defined_terms, and the defined and behavior-naming case is accepted. The reading.rs unit tests pass.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the check, the 7bf8 reading with no 'Term ladder:' line is accepted (`refusing_check` returns None), so the refuse case reports a mismatch. Without the definition-and-behavior pass logic, the accepted case would be refused. Because the first half of each pair (undefined refused) and the second half (defined accepted) both run, the check cannot be a blanket refusal.
